sophie_support: FYI KB Corp reported 500s for token refresh on their Dedicated cluster after yesterday's infra rollout. They say ~15% of requests fail, customer is hitting SLAs. Can we triage and decide hotfix vs next release?

maria_pm: Thanks Sophie. Do we know if it's regression from the infra change or a model change? Customer says it started ~20:10 UTC.

jon_eng: looking now. initial logs point to auth handshake timeout with our edge proxy. stacktrace shows: 
```
ERROR  | auth | TimeoutError: handshake exceeded 30s
  at ProxyHandler._connect (proxy.js:412)
  at processTicksAndRejections (internal/process/task_queues.js:95)
```

jon_eng: hypothesis: upstream cert rotation + our retry logic -> 2x latency -> hits 30s threshold. I can try a config tweak (increase timeout to 60s) and patch edge proxy on Dedicated nodes.

maria_pm: So options: 1) hotpatch config on KB's Dedicated pool (fast) 2) revert infra change (broad, slower) 3) include fix in next release (unsafe for SLA). Thoughts on risk & rollout?

priya_rel: For a hotpatch we need cherry-pick -> validation -> canary -> ramp. We do canary in prod by routing 5% of KB traffic first, monitoring errors for 15m, then 25%. We need a signed-off rollback plan. I can own coordination if Eng provides patch.

alex_sales: KB is on an enterprise plan with 99.95% SLA and legal already pinged us. They want an ETA and comms to their NOC. If hotfix is low-risk, they prefer immediate.

li_sre: Capacity note: their Dedicated pool is behind a standalone gateway. Canary routing means touching RG config and env var TTLs. We should schedule a brief maintenance window (15m) and pre-warm canary nodes. Also add an ephemeral alert rule for increased 5xx.

jon_eng: I can prepare a minimal change: bump handshake timeout to 60s and tighten the backoff to avoid retry storms. Code change is ~6 lines. Will open a PR and mark for cherry-pick to release/production.

oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0421-1987 (linked to support-73421). Assigned to jon_eng and li_sre. :rotating_light:

maria_pm: Decision: proceed with hotpatch (patch + canary). Rationale: customer SLA, easy small surface area change, low regression risk. Next-release inclusion as follow-up to make retry logic more robust.

priya_rel: Hotpatch plan (high level):
- jon_eng: open PR + test in staging (owner)
- li_sre: prepare canary routing and monitoring playbook (owner)
- priya_rel: schedule canary windows and comms, own rollback decision (owner)
- sophie_support: notify KB NOC and provide expected timeline (owner)

priya_rel: Canary steps:
1) Cherry-pick PR to production branch `release/prod`
2) Deploy to a canary subset: set `kbcorp.canary_percent=5` in RG config
3) Monitor `kbcorp.5xx_rate` and `auth.handshake_latency` for 20m
4) If stable -> ramp to 25% -> monitor 30m -> full rollout
5) rollback command (if >1% increase in 5xx over baseline):
```
# rollback
kubectl -n redwood rollout undo deployment/edge-proxy --to-revision=<prev>
```

jon_eng: I'll open the PR now and add a smoke test to hit the handshake path. ETA PR in 25m.

sophie_support: I'll ping KB NOC immediately and set expectation: maintenance window ~45-90m, updates every 30m. Will add KB contact list to the incident.

alex_sales: Please copy me on comms to KB NOC. I'll prepare a customer note template (status + ETA + mitigation).

li_sre: I'll add ephemeral alert: `query: rate(5xx{customer="kbcorp"}[5m]) > baseline*1.01` and a dashboard link. Also pre-create a rollback runbook in the incident doc.

maria_pm: Scope note: hotpatch is config + backoff tweak only. If we discover deeper auth cert bugs, we revert and escalate to a full incident postmortem and include in next release.

priya_rel: Final ask: confirm owners and add timers to the incident. Owners: jon_eng (patch + PR), li_sre (canary & monitoring), priya_rel (rollout coordinator), sophie_support (customer comms).

jon_eng: confirmed. PR: https://github.com/redwood/edge-proxy/pull/4982 (WIP) :hourglass_flowing_sand:

sophie_support: ACK. Notifying KB now.

alex_sales: Thanks all. Keep me in loop if we hit escalation.

maria_pm: Great — let's treat this as P1 for KB but keep internal comms light unless rollout fails. We'll reconvene in the incident channel after canary verification. :thumbsup:

oncall-bot: Incident update: INC-2026-0421-1987 -> status: in_progress.

(maria_pm added reaction :eyes:)
